body.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) and every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), a choice of \(K_{\alpha}\) depending only on the supplied radii and fixed class constants makes \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\) uniformly honest: \(\inf_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\), with \(\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})]\le C_{\alpha}\rho_n\). Conversely every uniformly honest rule \(C_n\in\mathcal I_n\), including every rule using the public functions and certified radii, has worst-case expected length at least \(c_{\alpha}\rho_n\), so \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\).
body.justification: Risk optimality alone does not answer the inferential price; this theorem makes honest expected length obey the same frontier.
body.gap: Rothe2017RobustCI uses finite-cell small-sample structure, Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves asymptotic Wald validity, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1, proves asymptotic normality after bias-corrected trimming; none calibrates the four-channel minimax bias radius or proves a matching honest-length converse.
body.consumer: Applied work that must retain the full population can report an honest bias-aware interval rather than trim the target or invoke a Gaussian approximation in a bias-dominated regime.
